explanation: Reduce the shift modulo the list length. Link the old tail to the old head, then break that cycle immediately before the new head, preserving every original node.
timeComplexity: O(n) Count the n nodes, then walk at most n links to the cut.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Length and a fixed number of node pointers suffice.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/list_cyclic_right_shift.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Reducing k modulo the length removes complete rotations. After temporarily joining tail to head, the new head is exactly length−k links after the old head. Cutting immediately before it yields the required order and visits each original node once, without creating copies.
walkthrough: For [1,4,7,9] shifted right by 5, reduce 5 modulo 4 to 1. The new head is 9 and its predecessor 7 becomes the tail, producing [9,1,4,7].
edgeCases: A multiple of the length preserves the head and links.
The result must end in null rather than retain the temporary cycle.
